item.title: ICE wasted millions in rapid push to expand detention capacity, watchdog finds
item.description: With an unprecedented budget, ICE spent billions in a rush to expand its detention network, wasting millions in the process, the Government Accountability Office found.

item.title: Tasia Fortune's hanging was "staged" after her death, police say
item.description: Authorities haven't disclosed the exact cause of Fortune's death, but they did rule it a homicide and have arrested two men.

item.title: Trump to hold midterm rallies in Alabama and Oklahoma
item.description: With less than six weeks until the November midterm elections, President Trump is set to campaign in the reliably red states of Alabama and Oklahoma. Political strategists Joel Payne and Kevin Sheridan join "The Takeout" to examine the president's avoidance of battleground states.

item.title: Software developer says there's a "dangerous gap opening up" between AI power and alignment
item.description: News broke this week that a rogue artificial intelligence agent hacked Australia's health care database, and no notice was given for months. Matt Calkins, CEO and co-founder of Appian, which develops software to maximize AI integration, joins to unpack the week's AI headlines.

item.title: Cook Political Report shifts 15 House races toward Democrats
item.description: The Cook Political Report shifted 15 House seat ratings toward Democrats on Friday and said it was almost impossible for Republicans to retain control of the House of Representatives. VoteHub head of data science Zach Donnini joins to discuss.

item.title: CEO of company behind FAA's new AI tool explains how the technology works
item.description: Washington, D.C., airports are debuting a new artificial intelligence tool designed to help air traffic controllers and airlines with future scheduling and weather issues. Air Space Intelligence CEO Phillip Buckendorf, whose company developed the system, joins "The Takeout" to explain how it works.

item.title: Supreme Court again blocks Missouri's new House map that favored GOP
item.description: The Supreme Court said in an unsigned decision that ordering Missouri to restore its 2025 map "would usher in electoral chaos."

item.title: Iran leader says "everything will return to the way it was" if U.S. recommits to terms in June deal
item.description: CBS News chief foreign affairs correspondent and "Face the Nation" moderator Margaret Brennan interviewed Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Friday in a network exclusive. Brennan joins "The Takeout" to unpack her conversation with the leader.

item.title: Facebook found liable for deceiving users in Cambridge Analytica case
item.description: The two-week trial in New Mexico centered on accusations Facebook deceived users about a data breach.

item.title: Pittsburgh doctor killed while he slept remembered as "a true angel on Earth"
item.description: Dr. Idris Evans, the Pittsburgh doctor killed in a violent home invasion, is being remembered for his kindness and compassion.

item.title: Hurricane Nolo could cause "catastrophic" flooding in Hawaii, forecasters warn
item.description: A hurricane watch is in effect for Hawaii County due to the storm, which could dump up to 3 feet of rain on Hawaii's Big Island.

item.title: The New York Film Festival returns with obsessions, deceptions and monsters
item.description: Challenging documentaries and award-winning features are among the offerings of New York City's leading cinema event, starring such luminaries as Pedro Pascal, Adam Driver, Scarlett Johansson, Julianne Moore and Godzilla.

item.title: Trump told Xi that aiding Iran was totally unacceptable, U.S. ambassador to China says
item.description: President Trump on Friday wrapped up his multi-day summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping. CBS News senior White House correspondent Weijia Jiang reports. Then, former U.S. Ambassador to China Nicholas Burns joins with analysis.

item.title: Voting now open for round two of Fat Bear Week after turnout crashes portal
item.description: Round two of voting in Fat Bear Week 2026 has kicked off to overwhelming public interest, with the event portal crashing earlier this week. Mike Fitz, a resident naturalist at Explore.org, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: ICE wasted millions in taxpayer dollars in rush to expand detention capacity, watchdog says
item.description: The Government Accountability Office reports that Immigration and Customs Enforcement wasted millions of taxpayer dollars in a rush to expand its detention capacity. CBS News data journalist Julia Ingram has the details.

item.title: Broadview 6 prosecutor retires under protest, blames U.S. attorney
item.description: Sheri Mecklenburg resigned from the Department of Justice this week, penning a scathing letter in which she said U.S. Attorney Andrew Boutros "personally directed" the Broadview 6 prosecution that she says ended her career.

item.title: Soaring U.S. diesel prices slam local communities as fuel costs surge
item.description: The surge in diesel prices this year is putting a financial squeeze on schools, farms and small businesses around the U.S.

item.title: Hurricane Nolo could bring catastrophic and life-threatening floods to Hawaii, forecasters warn
item.description: Hurricane Nolo is getting stronger as it approaches Hawaii. CBS News correspondent Carter Evans is in Pahala with more. Then, meteorologist Jessica Burch joins with the latest forecast.

item.title: How GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are changing fast-food menus
item.description: Chipotle, McDonald's and Shake Shack are among the restaurant chains revamping their menus as more consumers go on weight-loss drugs.

item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Sept. 27)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Book excerpt: "The Steps" by Sylvester Stallone
item.description: In his memoir, the actor writes of his early struggles, leading to writing his screenplay for the Oscar-winning hit "Rocky."

item.title: "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" guests for Sept. 27, 2026
item.description: This week's guests include Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Louisiana Sen. John Kennedy, Connecticut Rep. Jim Himes and Alexander Yui, Taiwan's representative to the U.S.

item.title: Supreme Court lets Trump administration use SAVE database for now
item.description: In a 6-3 decision, the Supreme Court sided with the Trump administration in its push to use a controversial database to review state voter rolls for potential noncitizens.

item.title: Ready or not, here come the AI gadgets, from "charms" to smart speakers
item.description: Meta, Microsoft and other major tech companies are developing a range of AI products for consumers, from wearables to speakers.

item.title: Iran proposes a 7-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Iran's president says Tehran wants a deal with the U.S. before November's midterm elections, as the regime puts an offer on the table.

item.title: A U.S. doctor survived a deadly strike in Gaza. Why he plans to go back.
item.description: Dr. Feroze Sidhwa was working at Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis when an Israeli strike hit the surgical unit he was in.

item.title: Minnesota sailor returns from USS Lincoln duty to find apartment ransacked
item.description: A Minnesota native who had been serving aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln for nearly 10 months came home to an upsetting surprise.

item.title: Duckworth slams Trump's "foolhardy plan" to make triumphal arch a military complex
item.description: Democratic Sen. Tammy Duckworth of Illinois is demanding the Pentagon and Federal Aviation Administration reject President Trump's call to convert plans for a massive triumphal arch into a "top grade Military Complex."

item.title: New Trump-focused "Love Me" ad campaign paid for by taxpayers hits airwaves
item.description: Ads promoting President Trump and paid for by American taxpayers are now airing on network and national cable.

item.title: Mistress testifies in trial of "American Idol" contestant charged in wife's murder
item.description: Caleb Flynn, a former "American Idol" contestant, is charged with killing his wife Ashley Flynn in February and then staging the crime scene.
